sentences.text: This bail application is filed under section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').
2. Petitioner is the 1st accused in Crime No.458/2025 of Cherthala Police Station registered for the offences punishable under Sections 409, 468, 471, 420 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

3. According to the prosecution pursuant to a conspiracy by the accused to misappropriate money from KSFE, the second accused forged a salary certificate impersonating the first accused as the Headmistress of Town LP School, Cherthala and the third accused, confirmed the document and based on which, a loan amount of Rs.3,75,000/- was granted to the first accused.
The second accused also forged salary certificates and documents of sureties for the purpose of availing a chitty from KSFE and the accused thereby committed the offences alleged.

4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor as well as the Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
5.

Petitioner is alleged to have forged salary certificates 2025:KER:40416 which were approved by the 2nd accused and availed a personal loan of Rs. 3,75,000/-. after keeping the salary certificate as a security.
However, it was later revealed that the 2nd accused, whose salary certificate was kept as security, was not even employed in the school and therefore the offences were alleged to have been committed.

6. In Ashok Kumar v. State of Union Territory Chandigarh [2024 SCC OnLine SC 274], it has been held that a mere assertion on the part of the State while opposing the plea for anticipatory bail that custodial interrogation is required would not be sufficient and that the State would have to show or indicate more than prima facie case as to why custodial interrogation of the accused is required for the purpose of investigation.

sentences.text: In the instant case, the State has not been able to convince this Court that custodial interrogation is necessary.
7. Petitioner is a lady.
She is alleged to have conspired with the other accused who are also women.
Though the nature of allegations indicate serious offences as having been committed, I am of the view that the custodial interrogation of the petitioner can be avoided.
However, the petitioner has to subject herself for interrogation.

sentences.text: On a consideration of the circumstances arising in the case, this Court is of the view that though the allegations are serious in nature, custodial interrogation of the petitioner is not required.

Further, 2025:KER:40416 having regard to the nature of the offence and the severity of punishment,
this Court is of the view that the petitioner is entitled to be released on pre- arrest bail, subject to conditions.

Accordingly, this application is allowed on the following conditions:
(a) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer on 20.06.2025 and shall subject himself to interrogation.

(b) If after interrogation, the Investigating Officer proposes to arrest the petitioner, then, he shall be released on bail on him executing a bond for Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum before the Investigating Officer.
(c) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer as and when required and shall also co-operate with the investigation.
(d) Petitioner shall not intimidate or attempt to influence the witnesses; nor shall he tamper with the evidence or contact the victim or her family members;
(e) Petitioner shall not commit any similar offences while he is on bail.
(f) Petitioner shall not leave India without the permission of the Court having jurisdiction.

In case of violation of any of the above conditions or for modification or deletion of the condition the jurisdictional Court shall be empowered to consider such application, if any, and pass appropriate orders in accordance with the law, notwithstanding the bail having been granted by this Court.
